Open with a substantial class recovery while keeping fees separate and subject to court review. Avoid clear sailing and ensure any fee not approved benefits the class, terms that are more defensible in a public negotiation transcript.

This structure is easier to defend on the public negotiation transcript.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The parties negotiated the class relief and attorneys’ fees together from the outset. Hargrove Lane’s opening proposal was a $28 million class fund, distributed automatically, plus $7 million in fees and expenses, with no clear-sailing agreement and any unawarded fees going to the class. Brightline proposed a $22 million automatic class fund and $5 million in fees and expenses on the same fee-protection terms. Hargrove Lane then countered with a $25 million automatic class fund and $5.5 million in fees and expenses, again with no clear sailing and any unawarded fees going to the class. Brightline accepted that counterproposal. The resulting agreement provides a $25 million class fund, automatic distribution, and a $5.5 million fee-and-expense request subject to court approval; Brightline may oppose the request, and any fees not awarded will go to the class.
